# Press Release


**SCHMID Launches QuantumLine P+ for Void-Free Bottom-Up Copper Filling of Through-Glass Vias**


**FREUDENSTADT** , **Germany** , November 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) – SCHMID Group N.V. (NASDAQ: SHMD) (the “Company” or “SCHMID”), a leading global provider of advanced manufacturing equipment and solutions for the electronics industry, today announced the launch of QuantumLine P+, a panel-level plating platform for the metallization of through-glass vias (TGV) in glass core substrates. QuantumLine P+ uses a bottom-up copper filling process that fills vias void-free at aspect ratios of up to 50:1 and hence addresses one of the critical process steps on the industry’s path from pilot lines to volume manufacturing of glass core substrates.


**Why TGV Metallization Matters**


Glass core substrates are expected to become a key enabler for the next generation of AI processors and high-performance computing. Glass offers a flat, dimensionally stable core for larger packages and finer interconnects. The electrical connection through the core is made by through-glass vias, which have to be filled with copper reliably and without voids.


As via aspect ratios increase, conventional conformal and bridge-fill plating approaches reach their limits. Seams and voids inside the via put electrical performance and long-term reliability at risk, and thick copper overburden on the panel surface adds cost in the following planarization step.


**Bottom-Up Filling on Panel Level**


In the QuantumLine P+ process, copper grows from the bottom of the via upward. The via is filled completely and void-free at aspect ratios of up to 50:1, with a uniformity of ±6% across the panel Uniformity and throughput is another key advantage of the SCHMID solution. The QuantumLine P+ delivers outstanding plating uniformity for any design and via density at 4-5 times higher throughput compared to conventional plating systems. The process is designed for panel sizes of 510x515mm and glass thicknesses of 200µm to 1500 µm.


The reliability of the filled vias has been confirmed in thermal cycling tests (TCT).


**Part of an Integrated Glass Core Process Chain**


QuantumLine P+ completes SCHMID’s portfolio for glass core substrates. QuantumLine H+ covers TGV formation by wet etching and ultra-clean processing. PlasmaLine provides the seed layer by vacuum metallization. InfinityLine L+ planarizes the panel by chemical-mechanical polishing after via fill. With its combined expertise in wet processing, plating and vacuum metallization on panel level, SCHMID supports customers along the critical process chain, from TGV formation and metallization to build-up layers.


In November 2026, SCHMID announced an order for key wet-process equipment for South Asia’s first glass substrate manufacturing facility. The launch of QuantumLine P+ extends the Company’s offering for the main production step of glass cores with copper via filling.


**Availability**


QuantumLine P+ is available for order as of December 2026. Customer sampling and process demonstrations are offered at SCHMID’s technology center in Freudenstadt, Germany.


**Executive Statement**


“Glass core substrates are moving from qualification to industrial scale, and the metallization of through-glass vias is one of the steps that decides whether this works in volume. With QuantumLine P+ we fill vias from the bottom up, void-free, at aspect ratios that conformal plating cannot reach reliably.


Together with our platforms for TGV etching, seed layer preparation and planarization, we now cover the critical process chain for glass core on panel level. That gives our customers one partner for these steps with highest level of integration and a faster path from development to production,” said Christian Schmid, Chief Executive Officer of SCHMID Group.

**About the SCHMID Group**


The SCHMID Group is a global leader in providing advanced equipment and process solutions for the high-tech industry, with a strong focus on electronics and semiconductor-related applications. Headquartered in Freudenstadt, Germany, and founded in 1864, SCHMID employs more than 800 people worldwide and operates technology centers and manufacturing facilities in Germany and China, as well as sales and service locations globally.


SCHMID develops customized systems and process solutions for the production of substrates, printed circuit boards and other electronic components. Its portfolio addresses a range of high-growth applications, including Advanced Packaging, semiconductor-related technologies, AI-driven electronics, printed circuit boards, substrates and glass-based technologies.


SCHMID’s solutions enable customers to achieve high technology levels, high yields, low production costs, maximum efficiency, quality, and sustainability in advanced manufacturing processes.
